A1.justification: Both readable, complete ten-page PDFs describe SSHNet and support comparison of their text, equations, tables and figures. Neither contains appendix pages; separately referenced supplementary material is unavailable and is not assumed to have been deleted.

before.justification: v3 reports original ablations, five-dataset homography comparisons and cross-dataset distillation evaluations in Tables 1–5, with qualitative results in Figure 7.

after.justification: v5 retains these quantitative experiments and adds original self-supervision, transfer-direction and real-world evaluation results in Tables 1, 4 and 7.

M1.justification: The two-network framework, split optimization, two-branch self-supervision, homography feature loss and teacher–student distillation remain unchanged. Equations 1–7 describe the same procedures; the new optimization schematic and transfer-direction ablation do not establish a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: The original five datasets and cross-dataset evaluations are retained. Section 5.5 adds natural RGB/NIR and Flash/no-flash pairs without perfect homography alignment, plus UDIS-derived RGB/TIR pairs with parallax. This substantially extends evaluation beyond simulated homographies and introduces thermal-image coverage.

E2.justification: The main benchmark retains identical comparator membership in v3 Table 4 and v5 Table 5. v5 adds pure self-supervised learning to Table 1 and compares SSHNet-IHN against identity alignment and SCPNet on UDIS-TIR in Table 7. CrossHomo and DMHomo are added citations, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The existing 128 × 128 images, [-32, 32] corner perturbations, MACE metric and ACE-below-5-pixels evaluation remain unchanged. Added experiments introduce reversed transfer directions, a pure self-supervision control and UDIS-TIR evaluation using PSNR and SSIM computed on RGB images before modality transfer.

E4.justification: v5 substantially broadens diagnostic and robustness evidence through a pure self-supervision control, bidirectional modality-transfer ablations and tests on real scenes that violate perfect homography alignment. Existing architecture, loss and generalization analyses remain. The comparative qualitative case study in v3 Figure 7 is absent from the supplied v5.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. v5 continues the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The main benchmark and cross-dataset table values are unchanged. New findings include pure self-supervision MACE 24.60 versus SSHNet's 2.94, and OPT-to-SAR versus SAR-to-OPT errors of 2.94 versus 4.28. On the new UDIS-TIR evaluation, SSHNet-IHN reports PSNR/SSIM of 20.05/0.728 versus identity's 12.92/0.306, while SCPNet does not converge. These extend the findings to new conditions; v3 Figure 7's per-example results are no longer supplied.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, losses and optimization objectives in Equations 1–7 are retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations appear; the additional schematic explains the existing optimization.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims, including the 47.4% and 85.8% OPT-SAR error reductions against MHN and LocalTrans. Replacing 'redefinition' with 'reformulation' changes terminology rather than scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly attributes SCPNet's iterative-architecture convergence difficulty to its lack of an explicit solution for cross-modal feature consistency. Section 5.2 explains richer-to-less-informative modality transfer as facilitating learning and convergence. Existing explanations of distillation generalization and its limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 newly documents constructing UDIS-TIR by applying a pretrained RGB-to-TIR translation network to UDIS RGB pairs. This adds data-processing information, although the translator and detailed configuration are unspecified. The code-access statement and existing architectural and loss descriptions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage expands to a dedicated image-to-image translation discussion covering Pix2pix, CycleGAN, UNIT, MUNIT, UNIT-DDPM and BBDM, alongside new CrossHomo and DMHomo discussion. v5 also adds references supporting the real-world datasets and removes the Szeliski and Zitova survey citations, substantially broadening the research context.

P1.justification: v5 changes 'redefinition' to 'reformulation' throughout, updates affiliations, adds acknowledgments and locally expands related work and experiments. The separate qualitative-comparison passage is removed, but the main section order, method exposition and most wording remain intact.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially revised: Figure 3 gains a straight-versus-split optimization schematic, and the large comparative grid in v3 Figure 7 is replaced by a real-world alignment mosaic. v5 also adds transfer-direction and UDIS-TIR tables, expands Table 1, adjusts Figure 4 and relocates Figures 5–6.

improvement.justification: The additional controls strengthen support for the design choices, and Section 5.5 supplies useful initial evidence beyond simulated homographies. Expanded related work and the optimization schematic improve context and clarity. These gains are limited by sparse details for the translated thermal evaluation and the loss of v3's comparative qualitative grid; the central method, claims and benchmark results remain unchanged.
